    Plots¶

    Plot functions, see Plots. They draw with matplotlib.

    forest ¶

    Forest plots (metafor's forest.rma, forest.default, addpoly.rma and addpoly.default).

    The layout logic follows the R code line by line: study rows are numbered k:1 from the top, the summary polygon sits at row -1 (prediction interval at -2), the axis limits are alim/xlim with the label and annotation areas reserved left and right of the plot, and the sizes of the arrow heads, CI end caps and summary polygons are fractions of the plot height.

    See https://wviechtb.github.io/metafor/reference/forest.rma.html and https://wviechtb.github.io/metafor/reference/addpoly.html, and Viechtbauer (2010), doi:10.18637/jss.v036.i03.

    ForestResult dataclass ¶

    ForestResult(
    ax: Axes,
    xlim: tuple[float, float],
    alim: tuple[float, float],
    at: FloatArray,
    ylim: tuple[float, float],
    rows: FloatArray,
    cex: float,
    cex_lab: float,
    cex_axis: float,
    ilab_xpos: FloatArray | None,
    ilab_pos: list[int] | None,
    textpos: tuple[float, float],
    areas: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None,
)

    What metafor's forest() returns invisibly, plus the axes drawn on.

    xlim/ylim are the limits of the plot region, alim the limits of the x axis, at the tick locations, rows the row of each plotted estimate, textpos the x positions of the study labels and annotations, areas the relative widths of the label, plot and annotation areas (forest of a fitted model only).

    style: str,

    | int
    | Sequence[str | int]
    | None = None,
    clim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
) -> ForestResult

    Forest plot of a fitted model (forest.rma), a cumulative analysis or of estimates with their variances (forest.default).

    Mirrors metafor's forest() and forest.rma(). Each study is drawn as a marker with a confidence interval. For a fitted model the summary estimate is added as a polygon below the studies (with an optional prediction interval); for a model with moderators the fitted value of each study is added as a polygon on its row. Arguments follow metafor's names (. becomes _). Indices are 0-based where they refer to studies (subset); rows and the numeric form of shade are plot rows as in R.

    Vector arguments of a fitted model (slab, ilab, pch, psize, colout, colci, order, a logical shade) must have one entry per study used in the fit or one per row of the original data (the entries of studies dropped for missing values are then removed, as in metafor). For a vector x they must have one entry per estimate.

    The differences from metafor are that predstyle='line2' is not available, that refline takes a single value, that predtail must be a number or a string such as '<2' and that slab=nan is only accepted for a vector x.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x RMAResult | RMAMVResult | FixedBinaryResult | RMALSResult | SelmodelResult | GLMMResult | CumulResult | ArrayLike

    A fitted model (from rma_uni and the other fitting functions), the result of cumul or a vector of estimates. A cumulative analysis is passed on to forest_cumul; the arguments slab, mlab, order, addfit, addpred, predstyle, showweights, predlim, colout and border then give a warning and are ignored. For a vector give the sampling variances (vi), standard errors (sei) or the CI bounds (ci_lb and ci_ub).

    		 required
    vi ArrayLike | None

    Sampling variances of the estimates in x (vector form only). Wins over sei.

    		 None
    sei ArrayLike | None

    Standard errors of the estimates in x (vector form only).

    		 None
    ci_lb ArrayLike | None

    Lower confidence interval bounds of the estimates in x (vector form only; with ci_ub). When given, the intervals are drawn from the bounds instead of from vi or sei; if neither of those is given the variances are derived from the bounds.

    		 None
    ci_ub ArrayLike | None

    Upper confidence interval bounds of the estimates in x (vector form only).

    		 None
    annotate bool

    Add the annotations (estimate and confidence interval) on the right of the plot. Default: True.

    		 True
    addfit bool | None

    Fitted model only: add the polygon of the pooled estimate (a model without moderators) or the polygon of the fitted value of each study (a model with moderators). Default: True. Ignored for a vector x.

    		 None
    addpred bool | str | int | Sequence[str | int] | None

    Add the prediction interval to the summary polygon (or, for a model with moderators, use the prediction instead of the confidence interval for the polygon of each study). True or False, or for an rma_mv model with several tau^2 values the levels of the inner factor to use. Has no effect for an equal-effects model. Default: False.

    		 None
    predstyle str | None

    Style of the prediction interval: 'line', 'polygon', 'bar', 'shade' (a bar shaded by the density of the predictive distribution) or 'dist' (the density itself, with the tails beyond the interval and the parts either side of predtail shaded); an unambiguous abbreviation is accepted. Setting it implies addpred=True; with moderators only 'line' is relevant (any other style gives a warning). Unlike R there is no 'line2'. 'shade' and 'dist' need transf to be one of numpy.exp, transf_ztor, numpy.tanh, transf_ilogit, plogis, transf_iarcsin, transf_iprobit, pnorm, transf_iahw or transf_iabt, or no transformation. Default: 'line'.

    		 None
    preddist tuple[ArrayLike, ArrayLike] | Mapping[str, Any] | None

    Predictive distribution to draw for 'shade' and 'dist': a pair of the values and the densities, or a mapping with the keys 'x', 'y' and optionally 'pi_lb', 'pi_ub' and 'level' (the bounds, else found numerically). Default: computed from the model.

    		 None
    showweights bool | None

    Fitted model: add the weights (in percent) of the studies as a column of the annotations; vector form: the weights are 1/vi, rescaled to percent. Not possible for the results of rma_glmm and selmodel. Default: False.

    		 None
    header bool | str | Sequence[str]

    True for the headings Study and, for the annotations, the estimate and CI level (for example Estimate [95% CI], dropped with annotate=False), False for none, a string for the left heading or a pair of strings for the left and right headings. Default: True.

    		 True
    xlim Sequence[float] | None

    Horizontal limits (left, right) of the plot region. Default: the CI bounds extended on both sides to leave room for the study labels, ilab columns and annotations.

    		 None
    alim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of the x axis (the axis and the polygons are drawn within them; intervals beyond them end in an arrow). Default: the range of at, else the pretty range of the CI bounds.

    		 None
    olim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits (lower, upper) that bound the estimates and the confidence and prediction interval bounds (values beyond them are set to the limits; useful for bounded measures). Default: no limits.

    		 None
    ylim Sequence[float] | None

    Vertical limits of the plot region. A single value sets the lower limit only. Default: from the rows of the studies, top and the summary rows.

    		 None
    predlim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits (lower, upper) of the predictive distribution drawn by predstyle='dist', on the plotted scale.

    		 None
    at ArrayLike | None

    Positions of the x-axis tick marks, on the scale that is plotted (after transf, before atransf). Positions outside alim are moved to its ends. Default: chosen from alim and steps.

    		 None
    steps int

    Number of tick marks of the x axis: exact when alim is given, otherwise approximate (as pretty chooses). Ignored when at is given. Default: 5.

    		 5
    level float | None

    Level of the confidence (and prediction) intervals: 95, 0.95 and 0.05 all give a 95% interval. Default: that of the model, or 95 for a vector x.

    		 None
    refline float | None

    Position of the dotted vertical reference line, or None for none. A single value (R also accepts several). Its line type is not affected by lty. Default: 0.

    		 0
    digits int | Sequence[float] | NDArray[floating]

    Number of decimals of the annotations, of the x-axis labels and of the weights, in this order. A single value is used for all three; two values give the third the value of the first. An integer (such as 2) drops trailing zeros from the axis labels, a float (such as 2.0) keeps them. Default: 2.

    		 2
    width int | Sequence[int] | None

    Minimum width (number of characters) of the annotation columns: one value for all columns or one per column. A column is never narrower than its longest entry. Default: the width of the longest entry.

    		 None
    xlab str | Sequence[str] | None

    Label of the x axis, or three (left end, centre, right end) or two (left and right end) labels. Default: the name of the measure (for example 'Log Risk Ratio'), else 'Observed Outcome', adjusted for transf and atransf.

    		 None
    slab Sequence[Any] | float | None

    Study labels, one per study. Default: the labels of the model, else Study 1, Study 2, .... For a vector x nan suppresses the labels; for a fitted model a labels vector cannot be suppressed that way.

    		 None
    mlab str | Sequence[str] | None

    Label of the summary polygon of a fitted model, or with a prediction interval drawn by a style other than 'line' a pair of labels for the polygon and the interval. Default: 'Random-Effects Model', 'Equal-Effects Model', 'Fixed-Effect Model' or 'Common-Effect Model' by the method of the model.

    		 None
    ilab Any

    Extra columns of information on the left of the plot: a vector, a matrix or a data frame with one row per study.

    		 None
    ilab_lab str | Sequence[str] | None

    Headings of the ilab columns, one per column.

    		 None
    ilab_xpos ArrayLike | None

    X positions of the ilab columns, one per column. Default: spread over the left part of the plot region.

    		 None
    ilab_pos int | Sequence[int] | None

    Alignment of the ilab columns (one value or one per column), as the pos argument of R's text(): 1 (below the position), 2 (to the left, so right-aligned), 3 (above) or 4 (to the right, so left-aligned). Default: centred.

    		 None
    order str | ArrayLike | None

    Order of the studies. A string, for a fitted model 'est', 'obs', 'yi' (by the estimates), 'prec' or 'vi' (by the sampling variances), 'fit' (by the fitted values), 'resid' or 'rstandard' (by the residuals or standardized residuals), 'abs.resid' or 'abs.rstandard'; for a vector x only 'est', 'obs', 'yi', 'prec' and 'vi'. Or a vector to sort by (increasing, or decreasing with decreasing=True). Default: the order of the data.

    		 None
    subset ArrayLike | None

    Vector form only (a fitted model raises an error): which estimates to show, a boolean array or 0-based indices (R: 1-based).

    		 None
    transf Callable[..., Any] | None

    Function applied to the estimates and to the confidence and prediction interval bounds (for example numpy.exp). Cannot be used together with atransf.

    		 None
    atransf Callable[..., Any] | None

    Function applied to the x-axis labels and to the annotations (the plot stays on the original scale, so numpy.exp gives a log scale). Cannot be used together with transf.

    		 None
    targs Any

    Additional arguments passed to transf or atransf.

    		 None
    rows ArrayLike | float | None

    Rows (vertical positions) of the studies, one per study, or a single value for the row of the first study (the others follow below it). Default: k for the first study down to 1.

    		 None
    efac float | Sequence[float]

    Vertical expansion factors, (CI end bars, arrows, polygon, prediction interval). One value is used for all; for a fitted model two values are (CI end bars and arrows, polygon and prediction interval) and three are (CI end bars, arrows, polygon); for a vector x two values are (CI end bars, arrows). A value of 0 leaves the element out. Default: 1.

    		 1
    pch int | Sequence[int]

    Plotting symbol of the study markers, an R code (0 to 6 and 15 to 25 are drawn; another code gives a filled circle); one value or one per study. Default: 15 (a filled square).

    		 15
    psize float | ArrayLike | None

    Sizes of the study markers: one value or one per study. Default: scaled by the square root of the weights of the model (for a vector x, of the precisions) within plim.

    		 None
    plim Sequence[float]

    (smallest, largest) marker size when scaled by weight; nan for one of them scales relative to the other as in R, and a third value sets a minimum (when the first is nan) or maximum (when the second is nan) size. Default: (0.5, 1.5).

    		 (0.5, 1.5)
    colout str | Sequence[str] | None

    Fitted model: colour of the study markers and, unless colci is given, of the interval lines; one value or one per study. Default: black. Not used for a vector x, where col does this.

    		 None
    colci str | Sequence[str] | None

    Colour of the confidence interval lines; one value or one per study. Default: that of the markers.

    		 None
    col str | Sequence[str] | None

    Fitted model: colour of the summary polygon (without moderators: up to four values for the polygon and the prediction interval, see below) or of the polygons of the fitted values (default '#CCCCCC'); the default for the summary polygon is black. Vector x: colour of the markers, interval lines and labels, one value or one per estimate (default black). For the prediction interval: col[1] is the colour of the interval (line, polygon or bar), for 'shade' col[1] and col[2] are the colours of the centre and the ends of the shading (defaults black and '#F2F2F2') and for 'dist' col[1] is the colour of the tails beyond the interval (default '#666666') and col[2] and col[3] are those of the regions on either side of predtail (defaults '#CCCCCC' and transparent).

    		 None
    border str | Sequence[str] | None

    Border colour of the summary polygon (border[0]) and of the prediction interval polygon, bar or curve (border[1]). For the polygons of the fitted values of a model with moderators the default is '#B3B3B3'; otherwise black.

    		 None
    shade bool | str | ArrayLike | None

    Shade rows. True or 'zebra' (alternate rows, counted from the bottom row, which is the last study; 'zebra1' is the same), 'zebra2' (the other rows) or 'all'; a boolean array with one entry per study; or numbers, the plot rows (as rows) to shade. Any other string raises an error. Default: no shading.

    		 None
    colshade str | None

    Colour of the shading. Default: '#E5E5E5' (light grey).

    		 None
    lty str | Sequence[str] | None

    Line types: for a fitted model (CI lines, prediction interval, horizontal lines), defaults 'solid', 'dotted' and 'solid' ('blank' removes the horizontal lines); for a vector x (CI lines, horizontal lines). A single value sets the first. The reference line is always dotted.

    		 None
    fonts str | tuple[str, int] | Sequence[str | tuple[str, int]] | Mapping[str, int] | None

    Font family and font of the study labels, the annotations and the ilab columns: a family such as 'serif', 'sans' or 'mono', a (family, font) pair with font 1 to 4 for plain, bold, italic, bold italic, a {family: font} mapping, or a sequence of up to three of these (one entry is used for all, two are completed with the first). Headings are always bold.

    		 None
    cex float | None

    Character expansion factor of the text and symbols. Default: 1, reduced when the number of rows would not fit on the axes (so the returned cex can be below 1).

    		 None
    cex_lab float | None

    Character expansion factor of the x-axis label. Default: the value of cex.

    		 None
    cex_axis float | None

    Character expansion factor of the x-axis tick labels. Default: the value of cex.

    		 None
    ax Axes | None

    Matplotlib axes to draw into. Default: the current axes.

    		 None
    predtail float | str | None

    Cut point of the shading for predstyle='dist', on the scale of the model (before transf): a number or a string such as '<2' or '>2' (the region below a '<' cut point, or above a '>' cut point or a plain number, is filled with col[2], the other region with col[3]). The strings 'lower' and 'upper' are not accepted. Default: 0, with the side towards zero filled with col[2].

    		 None
    annosym Sequence[str] | None

    Symbols of the annotations: left bracket, separator and right bracket (default ' [', ', ' and ']'), optionally a fourth for the minus sign (default '-') and a fifth for the space used in place of digits (default ' '). Three, four or five strings are accepted; another length raises an error.

    		 None
    tabfig int | None

    1, 2 or 3 replaces annosym by the symbols for fonts with tabular figures: thin spaces before the bracket and after the separator, a minus (1 and 3) or en dash (2) for the minus sign and an en space (1 and 2) or figure space (3) for the space. Other values are ignored.

    		 None
    textpos Sequence[float] | None

    (left, right) positions of the study labels (left aligned) and the annotations (right aligned); nan takes the limit of xlim. Default: the limits of xlim.

    		 None
    rowadj float | Sequence[float] | None

    Vertical adjustment of the study labels, the annotations and the ilab texts: one value (labels and annotations), two (the third is 0) or three. Default: 0.

    		 None
    top float

    Number of rows above the first study (for the headings). Default: 3.

    		 3
    at_lab Sequence[str] | None

    Labels of the tick marks, one per position. Default: the (atransf-transformed) positions.

    		 None
    xlabadj float | Sequence[float] | None

    Alignment of the left and right x-axis labels when two or three labels are given: 0 (left aligned), 1 (right aligned) or another value (centred), for the left label, the right label getting 1 minus that; or a pair for the two labels. Default: centred.

    		 None
    xlabfont int | Sequence[int]

    Font (1 to 4 as in fonts) of the x-axis labels: one value for all, or two with the second for the middle one of three labels. With one value the middle label gets that font, or the font from fonts when there are three labels. Default: 1.

    		 1
    decreasing bool

    Sort in decreasing order when order is a vector. Default: False.

    		 False
    measure str | None

    Vector form only: the measure used for the axis label and the header. Default: the attrs['measure'] of a pandas Series, else 'GEN'.

    		 None
    slab_null bool | None

    Vector form only: whether the labels are the default ones (which gives the study labels less room). Default: True when slab is not given.

    		 None
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    What to do with studies dropped for missing values (metafor's options(na.action=)): 'omit' (leave them out), 'pass' or 'exclude' (keep them as empty rows of the plot), or 'fail' (raise an error if there are any). Another value is not rejected and acts like 'omit'. Default: 'omit'.

    		 'omit'
    predtype str | None

    Type of prediction interval passed on to predict: 'default', 'simple', 'riley' or 't'.

    		 None
    pi_type str | None

    Old spelling of predtype.

    		 None
    addcred bool | str | int | Sequence[str | int] | None

    Old spelling of addpred; wins over it.

    		 None
    clim Sequence[float] | None

    Old spelling of olim; wins over it.

    		 None

    Type Description
    ForestResult

    A ForestResult (metafor returns the same values invisibly) with the fields ax, xlim, alim, at, ylim, rows,
    ForestResult

    cex, cex_lab, cex_axis, ilab_xpos, ilab_pos, textpos and areas (the relative widths of the label, plot and
    ForestResult

    annotation areas; None for a vector x). The markers, interval lines, polygons and texts are ordinary matplotlib artists on ax.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    NotSupportedError

    x is a location-scale model.

    Add polygons (summary estimates) to a forest plot (addpoly.rma, addpoly.predict.rma and addpoly.default).

    Mirrors metafor's addpoly(). Options not given (alim, digits, width, annotate, transf, atransf, targs, efac, fonts, cex, annosym, textpos, rowadj, olim, ...) are taken from the last forest call on the same axes; without one the limits of the axes are used. Unlike R there is no predstyle='line2' and no tabfig argument.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x RMAResult | RMAMVResult | FixedBinaryResult | RMALSResult | SelmodelResult | GLMMResult | PredictResult | ArrayLike

    A fitted model without moderators (its pooled estimate and confidence interval are drawn at row), the result of predict (its predicted values and intervals are drawn in rows, which then defaults to row), or a vector of estimates. For a vector give the sampling variances (vi), standard errors (sei) or the CI bounds (ci_lb and ci_ub).

    		 required
    vi ArrayLike | None

    Sampling variances of the estimates in x (vector form only).

    		 None
    sei ArrayLike | None

    Standard errors of the estimates in x (vector form only).

    		 None
    ci_lb ArrayLike | None

    Lower confidence interval bounds (vector form only; used with ci_ub, else vi or sei give the intervals).

    		 None
    ci_ub ArrayLike | None

    Upper confidence interval bounds (vector form only).

    		 None
    pi_lb ArrayLike | None

    Lower prediction interval bounds (vector form only). The prediction intervals of a vector x are drawn whenever pi_lb and pi_ub are both given, whatever addpred is.

    		 None
    pi_ub ArrayLike | None

    Upper prediction interval bounds (vector form only).

    		 None
    rows ArrayLike | float | None

    Rows (vertical positions) of the polygons, one per estimate, or a single value for the first (the others follow below it). Default: -1, -2, ... for a vector x, row for a predict result.

    		 None
    row float

    Row of the polygon of a fitted model. Default: -2.

    		 -2
    level float | None

    Confidence interval level: 95, 0.95 and 0.05 all give a 95% interval. Default: that of the model; for a vector x that of the last forest call, else 95.

    		 None
    annotate bool | None

    Add the annotation (estimate and interval) on the right. Default: as in the last forest call, else True.

    		 None
    addpred bool

    Fitted model or predict result: add the prediction interval. For a model without prediction interval (an equal-effects model) a warning is given and nothing is drawn for the interval. Default: False.

    		 False
    predstyle str | None

    Style of the prediction interval: 'line', 'polygon', 'bar', 'shade' or 'dist' (an unambiguous abbreviation is accepted; the last two draw the predictive distribution, see forest). Setting it implies addpred. Styles other than 'line' need prediction interval bounds, a single polygon and use two rows (the interval is drawn in the second, below the polygon). Default: 'line'.

    		 None
    predlim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits (lower, upper) of the predictive distribution drawn by predstyle='dist', on the plotted scale.

    		 None
    digits int | Sequence[float] | None

    Number of decimals of the annotation; only the first value of a sequence is used. Default: as in the last forest call, else 2.

    		 None
    width int | Sequence[int] | None

    Minimum width (number of characters) of the annotation columns. Default: the widths of the last forest call (so the annotations line up with those of the studies).

    		 None
    mlab str | Sequence[str] | None

    Label of the polygon(s), one string per polygon (a fitted model: one string). Default: the label for the method of a fitted model, none for a vector x.

    		 None
    transf Callable[..., Any] | None

    Function applied to the estimates and interval bounds before drawing. Default: as in the last forest call.

    		 None
    atransf Callable[..., Any] | None

    Function applied to the annotations only (the axis is not touched). Default: as in the last forest call. Cannot be used together with transf.

    		 None
    targs Any

    Additional arguments passed to transf or atransf. Default: as in the last forest call.

    		 None
    efac float | Sequence[float] | None

    Vertical expansion factors, (CI end bars, arrows, polygon, prediction interval). One value is used for all. For predstyle='line' two values are (polygon, prediction interval end bars and arrows) and three are (polygon, end bars, arrows); for the other styles two values are (polygon, prediction interval height) and three are (polygon, prediction interval height, arrows). A value of 0 leaves the element out. Default: as in the last forest call, else 1.

    		 None
    col str | Sequence[str] | None

    Colour of the polygon: one value per polygon. For a single polygon up to four values as for col of forest (polygon, then the colours of the prediction interval). Default: black.

    		 None
    border str | Sequence[str] | None

    Border colour of the polygon (one value per polygon; for a single polygon a second value is the border colour of the prediction interval). Default: black.

    		 None
    lty str | Sequence[str] | None

    Line types of the prediction interval for predstyle='line': (line, end bars); one value sets the line and leaves the end bars solid. Default: ('dotted', 'solid').

    		 None
    fonts str | tuple[str, int] | Sequence[str | tuple[str, int]] | Mapping[str, int] | None

    Fonts of the labels and annotations, as in forest (the first entry for the labels, the second for the annotations). Default: those of the last forest call.

    		 None
    cex float | None

    Character expansion factor. Default: that of the last forest call, else 1 or less, as small as the height of the axes needs.

    		 None
    constarea bool

    Draw the polygons with a constant area (the height shrinks as the interval widens) rather than a constant height. Default: False.

    		 False
    ax Axes | None

    Matplotlib axes to draw into. Default: the current axes.

    		 None
    preddist tuple[ArrayLike, ArrayLike] | Mapping[str, Any] | None

    Predictive distribution for 'shade' and 'dist', as in forest. Only for the numeric form, and for a single estimate.

    		 None
    predtail float | str | None

    Cut point of the shading for 'dist', as in forest (a number or a string such as '<2').

    		 None
    pi_se float | None

    Vector form only: standard error of the predictive distribution, for 'shade' and 'dist'. Taken from the model for a fitted model or predict result.

    		 None
    pi_dist str

    Vector form only: the predictive distribution, 'norm' (the default) or 't'.

    		 'norm'
    pi_ddf float | None

    Vector form only: degrees of freedom of the 't' distribution (must exceed 1 to draw it).

    		 None
    pi_level float | None

    Vector form only: level of the prediction interval, as level. Default: level.

    		 None
    alim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of the x axis: polygons are cut off at them. Default: taken from the last forest call, else the limits of the axes.

    		 None
    olim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits (lower, upper) that bound the estimates and interval bounds, as in forest. Default: taken from the last forest call.

    		 None
    annosym Sequence[str] | None

    Symbols of the annotations, as in forest (three, four or five strings). Default: as in the last forest call.

    		 None
    textpos Sequence[float] | None

    (left, right) positions of the labels and annotations. Default: taken from the last forest call, else the limits of the axes.

    		 None
    rowadj float | Sequence[float] | None

    Vertical adjustment of the labels and of the annotations; one value for both, or two. Default: as in the last forest call.

    		 None
    lcol str | Sequence[str] | None

    Colour of the prediction interval line, its end bars and arrows for predstyle='line'; one value or one per polygon. Default: black.

    		 None
    predtype str | None

    Type of prediction interval passed on to predict for a fitted model: 'default', 'simple', 'riley' or 't'.

    		 None
    pi_type str | None

    Old spelling of predtype.

    		 None
    addcred bool | None

    Old spelling of addpred (fitted model only); wins over it.

    		 None
    cr_lb ArrayLike | None

    Old spelling of pi_lb; wins over it.

    		 None
    cr_ub ArrayLike | None

    Old spelling of pi_ub; wins over it.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    Axes

    The matplotlib axes drawn into.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    an argument or the data is invalid: a fitted model with moderators; a predict result of scale values; both transf and atransf; a predstyle other than 'line' without prediction interval bounds or with several polygons; preddist with a fitted model; a length that does not match the number of polygons; no polygon left after dropping missing values.

    funnel ¶

    Funnel plots (metafor's funnel.rma and funnel.default).

    Plots the observed effects against a measure of their precision (standard error, variance, their inverses, sample size, weight, ...); for sei, vi, seinv and vinv the pseudo confidence-interval regions around the reference line are drawn (level may be a vector for contour-enhanced funnel plots, with shade the colours of the regions). For a fitted model with moderators the residuals are plotted; a trim-and-fill result (an :class:~metafopy.RMAResult with a boolean fill attribute) shows the imputed studies as open symbols.

    See https://wviechtb.github.io/metafor/reference/funnel.html, Sterne & Egger (2001), doi:10.1016/S0895-4356(01)00377-8 and Peters et al. (2008), doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2007.11.010.

    slab: tuple[str, ...],
    fill: NDArray[bool_] | None = None,
)

    The plotted coordinates (what metafor's funnel() returns invisibly) and the axes drawn on.

    x holds the observed outcomes (or residuals), y the values on the vertical axis, fill marks imputed studies of a trim-and-fill result (None otherwise).

    Funnel plot of a fitted model (funnel.rma) or of estimates with their variances (funnel.default).

    Mirrors metafor's funnel().

    yaxis is one of 'sei' (default), 'vi', 'seinv', 'vinv', 'ni', 'ninv', 'sqrtni', 'sqrtninv', 'lni' or 'wi'. level (a percentage; a vector draws several CI regions, a contour-enhanced funnel plot) defaults to the confidence level of the model (95 for the numeric form), shade colours the regions (back the background of the plotting region), refline is the reference line (the pooled estimate, or 0 for models with moderators and the numeric form), addtau2 adds the model's tau^2 to the sampling variances in the CI regions, label (True/'all', 'out' or the number of the most extreme studies) labels points with slab, and type selects the residuals plotted for models with moderators ('rstandard' or 'rstudent'). Pass ni (or fit the model with ni) for the sample-size axes. For a trim-and-fill result the imputed studies are drawn with symbol pch_fill (by default a circle with a grey fill). main is the title of the plot. legend is only approximated (a matplotlib legend). transf only warns, as in metafor (use atransf). na_action stands for R's options(na.action=): estimates with missing values are left out, except for 'fail', which stops; it has no effect on a fitted model.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x RMAResult | RMAMVResult | FixedBinaryResult | RMALSResult | SelmodelResult | GLMMResult | ArrayLike

    A fitted model (rma_uni, rma_mh, rma_peto, rma_glmm, rma_mv or a trim-and-fill result), or a vector of effect sizes (then give vi or sei, and ni for the sample-size axes).

    		 required
    vi ArrayLike | None

    Sampling variances of the effect sizes in x (vector form only; negative values are set to 0).

    		 None
    sei ArrayLike | None

    Standard errors of the effect sizes in x (vector form only; one of vi and sei is enough, vi takes precedence).

    		 None
    ni ArrayLike | None

    Sample sizes, for the sample-size yaxis values (vector form only; for a fitted model those stored in the model are used, and for a vector taken from an escalc result those stored with it).

    		 None
    subset ArrayLike | None

    Which of the effect sizes to plot: a boolean array or an array of 0-based indices (vector form only, ignored for a fitted model).

    		 None
    yaxis str

    Quantity on the vertical axis: 'sei' (default, standard errors), 'vi', 'seinv', 'vinv', 'ni', 'ninv', 'sqrtni', 'sqrtninv', 'lni' or 'wi' (weights in percent). The confidence regions are drawn only for 'sei', 'vi', 'seinv' and 'vinv'; the sample-size axes need sample sizes.

    		 'sei'
    xlim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of the horizontal axis as (low, high). Default: wide enough for the confidence region at the bottom of the plot and the points, extended by 10 percent on each side.

    		 None
    ylim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of the vertical axis as (low, high), in either order; they must be >= 0 (> 0 for 'seinv' and 'vinv'). Default: derived from the data. The axis is reversed (largest at the bottom) for 'sei', 'vi', 'ninv' and 'sqrtninv'.

    		 None
    xlab str | None

    Label of the horizontal axis. Default: derived from the effect size measure, or 'Residual Value' for a model with moderators.

    		 None
    ylab str | None

    Label of the vertical axis. Default: derived from yaxis.

    		 None
    slab Sequence[Any] | None

    Study labels (for label). Default: those of the model, or '1', '2', ... in the vector form. For a fitted model give one per row of the data passed to the model fit.

    		 None
    steps int

    Number of tick marks of the vertical axis (and of the horizontal grid lines). Default: 5.

    		 5
    at ArrayLike | None

    Positions of the tick marks of the horizontal axis (those outside its range are dropped). Default: chosen automatically.

    		 None
    atransf Callable[..., Any] | None

    Function applied to the horizontal-axis tick labels only (for example numpy.exp).

    		 None
    targs Any

    Additional arguments passed to atransf.

    		 None
    digits int | Sequence[int] | None

    Number of decimals of the tick labels: one integer for both axes or two (horizontal axis, vertical axis). Default: 2 and 3 (2 and 0 for yaxis='ni', 2 and 2 for 'wi').

    		 None
    level float | Sequence[float] | None

    Confidence level(s) in percent of the pseudo confidence regions (95 or 0.95 for 95 percent). A vector draws several regions, for a contour-enhanced funnel plot. Default: the level of the model (95 for the vector form).

    		 None
    addtau2 bool

    Add the model's tau^2 to the sampling variances in the confidence regions. Ignored, with a warning, for models with moderators, rma_mv and location-scale models. Default: False.

    		 False
    type str

    Residuals plotted for models with moderators: 'rstandard' (the default) or 'rstudent'.

    		 'rstandard'
    back str | None

    Colour of the plotting-region background. Default: light grey. (metafor's NULL, which suppresses it, is not supported.)

    		 None
    shade str | Sequence[str] | None

    Colour of the confidence regions; one colour per level (a single colour with several levels gives a ramp). Default: white; with several levels white for the first and shades of grey for the others.

    		 None
    hlines str | None

    Colour of the horizontal lines at the vertical-axis ticks. Default: white.

    		 None
    refline float | None

    Position of the vertical reference line, around which the confidence region is centred. Default: the pooled estimate, or 0 for models with moderators (where residuals are plotted) and the vector form.

    		 None
    lty Any

    Line type of the confidence region boundaries and of the reference line: one value for both or a pair (boundaries, reference line). Default: 3, dotted. Accepts R names ('solid', 'dashed', 'dotted', 'dotdash', 'longdash', 'twodash', 'blank'), R codes 0 to 6 or a matplotlib line style.

    		 3
    pch int | Sequence[int] | None

    Plotting symbol of the points (R's pch code), or one per study. Default: 19, a filled circle.

    		 None
    pch_fill int

    Plotting symbol of the imputed studies of a trim-and-fill result. Default: 21, a circle with border col and fill bg.

    		 21
    col str | Sequence[str] | None

    Border colour of the points, or one per study (a matplotlib colour). For a trim-and-fill result a pair (observed, imputed); a single colour then applies to the observed studies. Default: black.

    		 None
    bg str | Sequence[str] | None

    Fill colour of the points for symbols with a separate fill, or one per study; a pair (observed, imputed) for a trim-and-fill result. Default: light grey (a darker grey for the observed studies of a trim-and-fill result).

    		 None
    label bool | int | str

    Label points with the study labels: True or 'all', 'out' for the points outside the pseudo confidence region (all points for yaxis values without a region), or the number of the most extreme points (distance from refline) to label. Default: False.

    		 False
    offset float

    Distance of the labels from the points, as a fraction of the character size (R's text() offset). Labels sit right of points on or right of the reference line, left otherwise.

    		 0.4
    legend bool | str | dict[str, Any]

    Add a legend: True, a location (R's 'topright' and the like, or a matplotlib loc), or a mapping with the keys 'x' (the location), 'show' ('pvals', 'cis' or None) and 'studies' (bool); other keys are ignored. An approximation of metafor's legend: drawn with matplotlib. The study entries are omitted when pch, col or bg has one value per study.

    		 False
    ax Axes | None

    Matplotlib axes to draw into. Default: the current axes.

    		 None
    refline2 float | None

    Position of a second reference line, with its own confidence region for the four confidence-region yaxis values.

    		 None
    level2 float | None

    Confidence level in percent of the region around refline2. Default: the level of the model (95 for the vector form).

    		 None
    lty2 Any

    Line type of the second reference line and its region. Default: 3, dotted.

    		 3
    ci_res int

    Number of points used to draw the confidence region boundaries. Default: 1000.

    		 1000
    colref str | None

    Colour of the reference line(s). Default: grey.

    		 None
    colci str | None

    Colour of the confidence region boundaries. Default: grey.

    		 None
    colbox str | None

    Colour of the left and bottom axis lines (metafor's L-shaped box). Default: grey.

    		 None
    at_lab Sequence[str] | None

    Labels for the horizontal-axis tick marks, replacing the computed labels (give one per mark of at within the axis range).

    		 None
    measure str | None

    Vector form only: the effect size measure, used for the default horizontal-axis label. Default: the measure stored with x by escalc, if any.

    		 None
    main str | None

    Title of the plot. Default: none.

    		 None
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    What to do with missing values (R's options(na.action=)): 'omit' (the default), 'exclude', 'pass' or 'fail'. In the vector form, estimates with missing values are left out, except for 'fail', which raises; it has no effect on a fitted model.

    		 'omit'
    transf Any

    Not available, as in metafor: only gives a warning (use atransf).

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    FunnelResult

    The plotted coordinates and the axes (x, y, the study labels and the axes).

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    yaxis, type or na_action is unknown; ylim is out of range; no sample sizes are available for a sample-size yaxis; vi/sei is missing or the wrong length in the vector form; fewer than 2 effect sizes remain; slab, pch, col or bg has the wrong length; or values are missing and na_action='fail'.
    NotSupportedError

    yaxis='wi' for a model without weights, or a robust fit with moderators.

    L'Abbe plot of a model without moderators fitted to 2x2 table data or incidence rates (labbe.rma).

    Mirrors metafor's labbe().

    x is an rma_uni, rma_mh or rma_glmm fit (rma_peto fits have measure='PETO', which has no arm-level outcomes). rma_mh and rma_glmm fits keep the counts, and add/to default to the model's (for an rma_uni fit they do not, unlike metafor).

    The model's measure must be 'RR', 'OR', 'RD', 'AS', 'IRR', 'IRD' or 'IRSD'. A fitted RMAResult does not keep the raw counts, so they are taken from the columns ai, bi, ci, di (x1i, t1i, x2i, t2i for the rate measures) of the data the model was fitted to, or passed as the keyword arguments ai, bi, ci_counts (the ci counts; ci itself draws the confidence region as in metafor), di, x1i, x2i, t1i and t2i (column names or arrays). ci and pi shade the confidence and prediction interval of the line of the estimated effect (a colour string sets the colour), flip swaps the groups, psize/plim set the point sizes (default: proportional to the precision between plim), transf is applied to the arm-level outcomes, and add and to (see below for the defaults), lim/llim as in metafor. bty is the type of box around the plot ('o', 'l', '7', 'c', 'u', ']' or 'n'), which metafor passes on to plot(). na_action stands for R's options(na.action=); an unknown value raises, as in metafor, and every valid value gives the same result (metafor sets na.pass while it computes).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default

    A model without moderators fitted by rma_uni, rma_mh or rma_glmm to 2x2 table or rate data, with measure one of 'RR', 'OR', 'RD', 'AS', 'IRR', 'IRD' or 'IRSD' (rma_peto fits have measure='PETO').

    xlim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of the horizontal axis (the outcome in group 1) as (low, high). Default: the range of all the arm-level outcomes.

    		 None
    ylim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of the vertical axis (the outcome in group 2) as (low, high). Default: the range of all the arm-level outcomes.

    		 None
    lim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of both axes as (low, high); used instead of xlim and ylim.

    		 None
    xlab str | None

    Label of the horizontal axis. Default: derived from the measure, with (Group 1).

    		 None
    ylab str | None

    Label of the vertical axis. Default: derived from the measure, with (Group 2).

    		 None
    flip bool

    Swap the groups plotted on the two axes. Default: False.

    		 False
    ci bool | str

    Shade the confidence region of the line of the estimated effect; a colour string sets the colour (default light grey). Default: False.

    		 False
    pi bool | str

    Shade the prediction region of the line of the estimated effect; a colour string sets the colour (default lighter grey). Default: False.

    		 False
    grid bool | str

    Add a grid. True, False or a colour string for the grid lines. Default: False.

    		 False
    legend bool | str | dict[str, Any]

    Add a legend: True, a corner such as 'topleft' (or a matplotlib legend loc), or a mapping of which only 'x' (the location) is used. The default location is the lower right if the estimate is positive, else the upper left. An approximation of metafor's legend: drawn with matplotlib. Default: False.

    		 False
    add float | None

    Constant added to the cell counts (see escalc). Default: for rma_mh and rma_glmm fits the model's, otherwise 1/2 (0 for 'AS' and 'IRSD'); unlike metafor an rma_uni fit does not pass on its own add.

    		 None
    to str | None

    Which tables get add: 'all', 'only0', 'if0all' or 'none'. Default: for rma_mh and rma_glmm fits the model's, otherwise 'only0'.

    		 None
    transf Callable[..., Any] | None

    Function applied to the arm-level outcomes (and to the lines) before they are plotted, for example numpy.exp.

    		 None
    targs Any

    Additional arguments passed to transf.

    		 None
    pch int | Sequence[int]

    Plotting symbol of the points (R's pch code), or one per study. Default: 21, a circle with border col and fill bg.

    		 21
    psize float | Sequence[float] | None

    Sizes (expansion factors) of the points, a number or one per study. Default: proportional to the precision (inverse standard error of the difference), rescaled to plim.

    		 None
    plim Sequence[float]

    Range (min, max) of the point sizes when psize is not given, with an optional third value; NaN for min scales the largest to max (the third value then enforces a minimum size), NaN for max scales the smallest to min (the third value then enforces a maximum size). Default: (0.5, 3.5).

    		 (0.5, 3.5)
    col str | Sequence[str] | None

    Border colour of the points, or one per study (a matplotlib colour). Default: black.

    		 None
    bg str | Sequence[str] | None

    Fill colour of the points for symbols with a separate fill, or one per study. Default: grey.

    		 None
    lty str | Sequence[str] | None

    Line types of the line of equality (no effect) and of the line of the estimated effect, as a pair (one value serves both). Default: ('solid', 'dashed'); 'blank' suppresses a line. Accepts R names ('solid', 'dashed', 'dotted', 'dotdash', 'longdash', 'twodash', 'blank'), R codes 0 to 6 or a matplotlib line style.

    		 None
    ai ArrayLike | str | None

    Counts of the upper left cells (column name of the data the model was fitted to, or array); only needed if the model does not keep the counts and its data have no ai column.

    		 None
    bi ArrayLike | str | None

    Counts of the upper right cells (column name or array); as ai.

    		 None
    ci_counts ArrayLike | str | None

    Counts of the lower left cells (column name or array); as ai. (ci draws the confidence region, as in metafor.)

    		 None
    di ArrayLike | str | None

    Counts of the lower right cells (column name or array); as ai.

    		 None
    x1i ArrayLike | str | None

    Number of events in group 1 (rate measures); as ai.

    Draw the forest, funnel, radial and residual plots of a model (metafor's plot() of an rma.uni, rma.mh or rma.peto fit).

    Mirrors metafor's plot.rma.uni().

    For a model without moderators the panels are forest, funnel, radial and the standardized residuals (rstandard) of the studies in order; for a meta-regression the funnel plot shows the residuals and the radial plot is replaced by the standardized residuals against the fitted values. qqplot=True draws qqnorm (with seed for its envelope) instead of the last panel. The panels fill ax (default: the current axes) in a 2 x 2 grid, as par(mfrow = c(2, 2)) does. A selection model (rma.uni.selmodel) is drawn by plot_selmodel, which gets kwargs, as R's plot() dispatches to plot.rma.uni.selmodel. na_action stands for R's options(na.action=): with 'omit' (default) the last panel and the third panel of a meta-regression show the studies used in fitting, with 'exclude' and 'pass' every study of the subset (a gap where a value is missing), and 'fail' stops when studies were left out of the fit.

    plot_selmodel(
    x: SelmodelResult,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    ylim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    n: int = 1000,
    prec: str | float = 'max',
    scale: bool = False,
    ci: bool | str = False,
    reps: int = 1000,
    shade: bool | str = True,
    rug: bool = True,
    add: bool = False,
    lty: str | int | Sequence[str | int] = LINE_STYLES,
    lwd: float | Sequence[float] = (2.0, 1.0),
    seed: int | None = None,
    draw: bool = True,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    bty: str = 'o',
    col: str | None = None,
) -> SelPlotResult

    Draw the selection function of a selection model against the p-value.

    Mirrors metafor's plot.rma.uni.selmodel().

    prec fixes the precision at which the function is drawn ('min', 'max', 'mean', 'median' or a number). ci adds a confidence region: 'wald' transforms the Wald bounds of the selection parameters, 'boot' (or True) simulates reps parameter vectors from their estimated multivariate normal distribution (with NumPy's generator seeded by seed, so the bounds agree with metafor only up to simulation error). scale rescales the curve to the unit interval, shade fills the region, rug marks the observed p-values and add draws into existing axes. draw=False only computes the curve. bty (the type of box around the plot) and col (the colour of the lines) are passed on to plot() and lines() by metafor. The curve is returned as SelPlotResult.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x SelmodelResult

    A selection model from selmodel.

    		 required
    xlim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of the horizontal axis (the p-values for which the function is drawn), within 0 and 1. Default: the model's smallest p-value pval_min to 1 - pval_min, which is 0 to 1 unless the selection function or the pval.min control of selmodel sets a small positive minimum (1e-5 for some functions).

    		 None
    ylim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of the vertical axis as (low, high). Default: 0 to 1 for the bounded selection functions (halfnorm, halfnorm2, logistic, logistic2, negexp, negexp2, negexppow, power, power2), otherwise the range of the curve (and of the confidence region).

    		 None
    n int

    Number of p-values within xlim at which the function is computed. Default: 1000. For step functions the step points are added.

    		 1000
    prec str | float

    Precision at which a selection function that involves one is drawn: 'min' (the most precise study), 'max' (the default, the least precise study), 'mean', 'median' or a number (1 corresponds to 'max', smaller values to higher precision; the number is replaced by 1 if the model was fitted without the prec argument of selmodel).

    		 'max'
    scale bool

    Rescale the curve (and region) to the 0 to 1 range. Default: False.

    		 False
    ci bool | str

    Add a confidence region around the curve: False (the default), True or 'boot' (parametric bootstrap: reps parameter vectors are simulated from the estimated multivariate normal distribution of the selection parameters, with NumPy's generator, so the bounds agree with metafor only up to simulation error), or 'wald' (the curve at the Wald bounds of the parameter; for models with a single selection parameter and for step functions). Nothing is drawn if the model has no standard errors for the parameters.

    		 False
    reps int

    Number of simulated parameter vectors for the 'boot' region. Default: 1000.

    		 1000
    shade bool | str

    Shade the confidence region: True (the default, light grey), False or a colour.

    		 True
    rug bool

    Mark the observed p-values along the horizontal axis (not with add). Default: True.

    		 True
    add bool

    Add the curve to the existing axes without drawing a new frame, labels or rug. Default: False.

    		 False
    lty str | int | Sequence[str | int]

    Line types of the selection function and of the confidence region bounds, as a pair (a single value serves the curve and the bounds get 'dotted'). Default: ('solid', 'dotted'). Accepts R names ('solid', 'dashed', 'dotted', 'dotdash', 'longdash', 'twodash', 'blank'), R codes 0 to 6 or a matplotlib line style.

    		 LINE_STYLES
    lwd float | Sequence[float]

    Line widths of the selection function and of the confidence region bounds, as a pair (a single value serves the curve and the bounds get 1). Default: (2, 1).

    		 (2.0, 1.0)
    seed int | None

    Seed of NumPy's generator for the 'boot' region (not R's generator). Default: not seeded.

    		 None
    draw bool

    If False only compute the curve and do not draw (the returned ax is None). Default: True.

    		 True
    ax Axes | None

    Matplotlib axes to draw into. Default: the current axes.

    		 None
    bty str

    Type of box around the plot: 'o' (the default), 'l', '7', 'c', 'u', ']' or 'n' (none). Ignored with add.

    		 'o'
    col str | None

    Colour of the curve and of the confidence region bounds (the shading has its own colour shade). Default: black.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    SelPlotResult

    A SelPlotResult with the p-values xs, the selection function ys, the confidence bounds ys_lb and ys_ub (NaN without a
    SelPlotResult

    confidence region) and the axes ax (None if draw is false).

    Raises:

    the model has a truncated selection function or none; ci is unknown; xlim or ylim does not have two values or xlim is outside 0 to 1; prec is an unknown string; or ci='wald' is not possible for the model.

    slab: Sequence[Any] | None = None,

    offset: float | Sequence[float] = (1.0, 1.0),
    labsize: float = 1.0,
    lcol: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    lwd: float | Sequence[float] | None = None,
    lty: str | int | Sequence[str | int] | None = None,
    legend: bool | str | dict[str, Any] = False,
    xvals: ArrayLike | None = None,
    *,
    bty: str = 'o',
    las: int = 0,
    grep: bool = False,
    fixed: bool = False,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    xaxt: str = 's',
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'

    at_lab: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    box_lty: str = 'solid',
) -> RegplotResult

    Meta-analytic scatterplot of a meta-regression model (regplot.rma).

    Mirrors metafor's regplot().

    mod is the moderator on the horizontal axis (its name, or its 0-based position among the coefficients; it may be left out when the model has a single moderator). The regression line (pred) and the confidence (ci) and prediction (pi) bands are drawn for the other moderators set to their means; xvals gives the moderator values to predict at, and pred may be a PredictResult for those values. transf transforms the effects and the bands, atransf only the labels of the vertical axis, and olim limits the values drawn. The points have the cex psize (or the square roots of the weights rescaled to plim; give 'seinv' or 'vinv' to scale the inverse standard errors or variances instead). label labels the studies (True/'all', 'ciout'/'piout' for those outside the bands, a boolean array or 0-based indices), with offset the distance from the point in percent of the vertical range and labsize the text size. legend adds a legend (True, a location such as 'topright' or a dict with x and cex); box_lty is the line type of its frame ('blank' for none). at_lab gives the labels of the ticks at of the vertical axis (one per value of at, or per tick when at is not given) instead of the formatted values.

    bty ('o' or 'l') is the box type and las the orientation of the labels of the vertical axis (0 = parallel to it, 1 = horizontal). xaxt='n' leaves out the horizontal axis. grep=True makes a string mod a regular expression searched for in the coefficient names (which must find exactly one) and fixed=True a literal string instead (the grep and fixed arguments metafor reads through ...). na_action stands for R's options(na.action=): 'fail' stops when the regression line is drawn (pred=True) and studies were left out of the fit, the other choices give the same plot.

    x is a fit of rma, including location-scale models, of selmodel, of rma_mv or of rma_glmm; the bands are the predictions of the model, so no prediction interval is drawn where predict gives none (location-scale models). The sizes of the points are equal for the models without weights (selmodel and rma_glmm fits).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x RMAResult | RMAMVResult | FixedBinaryResult | RMALSResult | SelmodelResult | GLMMResult

    		 required

    Moderator on the horizontal axis: its name (matched exactly or as the start of one coefficient name), or its 0-based position among the coefficients (the intercept, if any, is position 0). May be left out when the model has a single moderator.

    		 True
    ci bool

    Draw the confidence band. Default: True.

    		 True
    pi bool

    Draw the prediction band (none is drawn, with a warning, where the model gives no prediction interval). Default: False.

    		 False

    Shade the bands: True (the default, light greys), False, or colour(s) for the confidence and prediction bands (a single colour serves both).

    		 True

    Limits of the horizontal axis as (low, high). Default: the range of the moderator.

    		 None
    ylim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of the vertical axis as (low, high). Default: the range of the (transformed) estimates and of the prediction band (if drawn) or confidence band, extended to include at.

    		 None

    Limits (low, high) of the moderator values for the regression line and bands. Default: the range of the moderator extended by 4 percent on each side.

    		 None

    		 None

    Positions of the tick marks of the vertical axis (on the transformed scale of transf, before atransf). Default: chosen automatically.

    		 2

    		 None
    pch int | Sequence[int]

    Plotting symbol of the points (R's pch code), or one per study used in the fit. Default: 21, a circle with border col and fill bg.

    		 21
    psize float | str | Sequence[float] | None

    Size (expansion factor) of the points: a number, one per study used in the fit, or 'seinv'/'vinv' to make the sizes proportional to the inverse standard errors or variances (rescaled to plim). Default: the square roots of the weights rescaled to plim (equal sizes for models without weights).

    Cumulative forest plot (forest.cumul.rma): one row per step of a cumul analysis.

    Mirrors metafor's forest.cumul.rma().

    The first row is labelled with the first study, the others with + and the added study (Study and its label when the model had no study labels). The plot is that of forest for a vector of estimates with confidence intervals: there is no summary polygon, the arguments mean what they mean there for a vector x (so col colours the markers, interval lines and labels) and the confidence level is that of the cumulative analysis. forest(cumul(res), ...) is the same call (with warnings for the arguments of the fitted-model form that this plot does not have).

    		 5
    refline float | None

    Minimum width (number of characters) of the annotation columns, one value or one per column. Default: the longest entry.

    		 None

    ilab Any

    Extra columns of information on the left: a vector, a matrix or a data frame with one row per step.

    		 None

    		 None

    		 None

    Alignment of the ilab columns, as the pos argument of R's text(): 1 (below), 2 (to the left, so right-aligned), 3 (above) or 4 (to the right, so left-aligned). Default: centred.

    Shade rows: True or 'zebra' (alternate rows from the bottom), 'zebra2' (the other rows), 'all', a boolean array with one entry per step, or numbers, the plot rows to shade. Default: no shading.

    plot_cumul ¶

    plot_cumul(
    x: CumulResult,
    yaxis: str | None = None,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    ylim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    xlab: str | None = None,
    ylab: str | None = None,
    at: ArrayLike | None = None,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    atransf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    digits: int | Sequence[int] | None = None,
    cols: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    grid: bool | str = True,
    pch: int = 19,
    cex: float = 1.0,
    lwd: float = 2.0,
    *,
    las: int = 0,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    addgrid: bool | str | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> PlotCumulResult

    Plot of the results of a cumulative meta-analysis (plot.cumul.rma).

    Mirrors metafor's plot.cumul.rma().

    The pooled estimates (horizontal axis) are plotted against the amount of heterogeneity (yaxis 'tau2', 'tau', 'I2' or 'H2'; 'tau2' unless the model is a fixed-effects one), joined in order by a line whose colour runs from the first of cols to the last (light to dark by default). transf transforms the estimates, atransf only the labels of the horizontal axis, digits are the digits of the labels of the two axes and grid draws the dotted grid (a colour for the lines of the grid; addgrid is the old spelling that metafor reads from ... and wins).

    na_action stands for R's options(na.action=): an unknown value raises, the others give the same result (metafor sets na.pass while it computes). With 'fail' missing values in the results stop the plot.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x CumulResult

    The result of cumul.

    		 required
    yaxis str | None

    Heterogeneity statistic on the vertical axis: 'tau2', 'tau', 'I2' or 'H2' (the first two need a random-effects model). Default: 'tau2' for a random-effects model, 'I2' for an equal-effects one.

    		 None
    xlim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of the horizontal axis as (low, high), in either order. Default: the range of the (transformed) pooled estimates.

    		 None
    ylim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of the vertical axis as (low, high), in either order. Default: the range of the heterogeneity statistic.

    		 None
    xlab str | None

    Label of the horizontal axis. Default: derived from the effect size measure.

    		 None
    ylab str | None

    Label of the vertical axis. Default: derived from yaxis.

    		 None
    at ArrayLike | None

    Positions of the tick marks of the horizontal axis (on the scale after transf, before atransf); the horizontal limits are widened to include them. Default: chosen automatically.

    		 None
    transf Callable[..., Any] | None

    Function applied to the pooled estimates before drawing. Not together with atransf.

    		 None
    atransf Callable[..., Any] | None

    Function applied to the labels of the horizontal axis only. Not together with transf.

    		 None
    targs Any

    Additional arguments passed to transf or atransf.

    		 None
    digits int | Sequence[int] | None

    Number of decimals of the tick labels of the horizontal axis and of the vertical axis: one integer for both or a pair (horizontal, vertical). Default: 2 and 3 for 'tau2'/'tau', 2 and 1 for 'I2'/'H2'.

    		 None
    cols Sequence[str] | None

    Colours (matplotlib colours) of the first and last step; the points and the line change from the first to the last. Only the first and last colour are used (metafor interpolates through all of them). Default: light grey to dark grey.

    		 None
    grid bool | str

    Draw the dotted grid; a colour string sets the colour of its lines. Default: True.

    		 True
    pch int

    Plotting symbol of the points (R's pch code). Default: 19, a filled circle.

    		 19
    cex float

    Expansion factor of the points. Default: 1.

    		 1.0
    lwd float

    Width of the line joining the steps. Default: 2.

    		 2.0
    las int

    Orientation of the vertical-axis tick labels: 0 (the default) parallel to the axis, any other value horizontal.

    		 0
    ax Axes | None

    Matplotlib axes to draw into. Default: the current axes.

    		 None
    addgrid bool | str | None

    Old spelling of grid (read from ... by metafor); wins over it when given.

    		 None
    na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

    What to do with missing values (R's options(na.action=)): 'omit' (the default), 'exclude', 'pass' or 'fail'; the first three give the same plot (steps with a missing estimate or statistic are left out), 'fail' raises when the results contain missing values.

    		 'omit'

    Returns:

    Type Description
    PlotCumulResult

    A PlotCumulResult with the axes ax, the plotted (transformed) pooled estimates estim, the heterogeneity statistic yval and the
    PlotCumulResult

    colour col of each step.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    x is not the result of cumul; yaxis or na_action is unknown, or yaxis needs a random-effects model; transf and atransf are both given; or 'fail' and results are missing.

    llplot ¶

    Plot of the likelihood functions of the individual studies (metafor's llplot).

    For measure='GEN' each study contributes the normal likelihood of its effect size yi with sampling variance vi; for measure='OR' the likelihood of the (log) odds ratio is the conditional one given the margins of the 2x2 table, which follows Fisher's non-central hypergeometric distribution (Fog 2008, doi:10.1080/03610910701790236). With scale=True every likelihood is rescaled to area one, so that the curves show how much information each study has about the effect. See https://wviechtb.github.io/metafor/reference/llplot.html and van Houwelingen et al. (1993), doi:10.1002/sim.4780122405.

    LlplotResult dataclass ¶

    LlplotResult(ax: Axes, xs: FloatArray, lls: FloatArray)

    The likelihoods drawn (what metafor's llplot() returns invisibly): lls[i, j] is the likelihood of study i at xs[j].

    Values outside of the (very wide) confidence interval of a study are NaN and not drawn.

    llplot ¶

    llplot(
    measure: str = 'GEN',
    yi: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    vi: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    sei: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    ai: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    bi: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    ci: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    di: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    n1i: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    n2i: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    data: Any = None,
    subset: ArrayLike | None = None,
    drop00: bool = True,
    xvals: int = 1000,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    ylim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    xlab: str | None = None,
    ylab: str | None = None,
    scale: bool = True,
    lty: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    lwd: float | Sequence[float] | None = None,
    col: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    level: float = 99.99,
    refline: float | None = 0,
    *,
    onlyo1: bool = False,
    addyi: bool = True,
    addvi: bool = True,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
) -> LlplotResult

    Plot the likelihood function of the true effect given the data of each study (llplot).

    Mirrors metafor's llplot().

    measure is 'GEN' (give yi with vi or sei) or 'OR' (give the counts ai, bi, ci, di, or ai, n1i, ci, n2i). Studies with no cases (or only cases) in both groups (drop00) are left out for 'OR'; if kept, they are drawn dotted, and tables with a single zero count dashed, as in metafor. xvals is the number of points of each curve, level the confidence level of the interval outside which the curves are not drawn, scale rescales each likelihood to area one, and lty, lwd and col are per study (by default the more precise studies get thicker and darker lines). refline draws a vertical line.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    measure str

    'GEN' (the default; give yi with vi or sei) or 'OR' (give the counts ai, bi, ci, di, or ai, n1i, ci, n2i).

    		 'GEN'
    yi ArrayLike | str | None

    Observed effect sizes (array or column name of data), for measure='GEN'.

    		 None
    vi ArrayLike | str | None

    Sampling variances (array or column name), for measure='GEN'.

    		 None
    sei ArrayLike | str | None

    Standard errors (array or column name), for measure='GEN'; an alternative to vi, which takes precedence.

    		 None
    ai ArrayLike | str | None

    2x2 table counts, upper left cell (array or column name), for measure='OR'.

    		 None
    bi ArrayLike | str | None

    2x2 table counts, upper right cell.

    		 None
    ci ArrayLike | str | None

    2x2 table counts, lower left cell.

    		 None
    di ArrayLike | str | None

    2x2 table counts, lower right cell.

    		 None
    n1i ArrayLike | str | None

    Size of group 1 (the row total of the first row); an alternative to bi (bi = n1i - ai).

    		 None
    n2i ArrayLike | str | None

    Size of group 2 (the row total of the second row); an alternative to di (di = n2i - ci).

    		 None
    data Any

    Data frame holding the variables named (as column names) in the other arguments.

    		 None
    subset ArrayLike | None

    Which studies to use: a boolean array or an array of 0-based indices (into the data, so lty, lwd and col still have one value per study of the whole data).

    		 None
    drop00 bool

    Drop studies with no cases (or only cases) in both groups (measure='OR'). If False they are kept and drawn dotted. Default: True.

    		 True
    xvals int

    Number of points at which each likelihood is evaluated. Default: 1000.

    		 1000
    xlim Sequence[float] | None

    plot_permutest ¶

    plot_permutest(
    x: PermutestResult | LSPermutestResult,
    beta: Sequence[int | str] | int | str | None = None,
    alpha: Sequence[int | str] | int | str | None = None,
    QM: bool = False,
    QS: bool = False,
    breaks: object = 'Scott',
    freq: bool = False,
    col: str | None = None,
    border: str | None = None,
    col_out: str | None = None,
    col_ref: str | None = None,
    col_density: str | None = None,
    trim: float = 0.0,
    adjust: float = 1.0,
    lwd: float | Sequence[float] = (2, 0, 0, 4),
    legend: bool | str = False,
    *,
    alternative: str | None = None,
    p2defn: str | None = None,
    stat: str | None = None,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    layout: object = None,
) -> PlotPermutestResult

    Plot the permutation distributions of a permutest result (plot.permutest.rma.uni).

    Mirrors metafor's plot.permutest.rma.uni().

    One panel is drawn per selected element, in the order of metafor: the omnibus test of the location coefficients (QM=True), the location coefficients, the omnibus test of the scale coefficients (QS=True) and the scale coefficients. Each panel is the histogram of the permuted test statistics (or coefficients), the observed value is a dashed line and the tails beyond it are filled with col_out. The theoretical null distribution and the kernel density estimate are omitted by default (their lwd is 0). A single-coefficient plot has no panel title.

    Trimming only affects the histogram; the kernel density estimate uses all permutations.

    For an omnibus test with a single degree of freedom (QM=True and one coefficient tested) the theoretical density is infinite at 0. That point is left out of the curve and of the y range, whereas metafor stops with an infinite ylim there.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x PermutestResult | LSPermutestResult

    The result of permutest; a location-scale permutation test gives LSPermutestResult.

    		 required
    beta Sequence[int | str] | int | str | None

    Location coefficients to plot, as names or 0-based positions (R: 1-based). A single name or position is allowed. Default None: all coefficients but the intercept (the intercept only when it is the only coefficient). [] selects none.

    		 None
    alpha Sequence[int | str] | int | str | None

    Scale coefficients to plot, selected as beta. Only used for LSPermutestResult; default None: all but the intercept.

    		 None
    QM bool

    Add the panel of the omnibus test of the location coefficients (ignored for an intercept-only model). Default: False.

    		 False
    QS bool

    Add the panel of the omnibus test of the scale coefficients (LSPermutestResult only). Default: False.

    		 False
    breaks object

    The breaks argument of R's hist(): a number of bins, a rule name or a vector of break points. Default: 'Scott'.

    		 'Scott'
    freq bool

    Draw counts instead of densities. Forces lwd[1] and lwd[2] to 0, so no curves are drawn. Default: False.

    		 False
    col str | None

    Fill colour of the histogram bars. Default: '#B3B3B3' (light grey).

    		 None
    border str | None

    Border colour of the bars. Default: '#E5E5E5' (lighter grey).

    		 None
    col_out str | None

    Fill colour of the bars in the tails beyond the observed value. Default: '#FF000080' (semi-transparent red).

    		 None
    col_ref str | None

    Colour of the theoretical null distribution. Default: '#4C4C4C' (dark grey). The dashed line at the observed value and the vertical line at zero are always black.

    		 None
    col_density str | None

    Colour of the kernel density estimate. Default: 'blue'.

    		 None
    trim float

    Fraction of the permutations dropped from the histogram, which must be below 0.5. The omnibus panels drop the upper trim fraction, the coefficient panels drop trim / 2 from each tail. Default: 0.

    		 0.0
    adjust float

    Bandwidth adjustment of the kernel density estimate, as the adjust argument of R's density(). Default: 1.

    		 1.0
    lwd float | Sequence[float]

    Line widths of the dashed line at the observed value, of the theoretical null distribution, of the kernel density estimate and of the vertical line at zero (coefficient panels only). A width of 0 leaves the element out. A single number is used for the first three and 4 for the last; two or three values are completed to four (the second is repeated for the third, the last defaults to 4). Default: (2, 0, 0, 4).

    		 (2, 0, 0, 4)
    legend bool | str

    True or a location (for example 'topleft') for a legend naming the curves; drawn in the first panel only and only when a curve is drawn. True places it at the top right. Default: False.

    		 False
    alternative str | None

    'two.sided', 'greater' or 'less'. Default: that of the test.

    		 None
    p2defn str | None

    Definition of the two-sided p-value, 'abs' or 'px2'. Default: that of the test.

    		 None
    stat str | None

    Statistic plotted, 'test' (z or t values) or 'coef' (coefficients). Default: that of the test.

    		 None
    ax Axes | None

    Matplotlib axes to draw into; the panels are laid out inside it. Default: the current axes.

    		 None
    xlim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of the horizontal axis of every panel. Default: the range of the histogram breaks. The plotted axis extends 4 percent beyond the limits, as in R.

    		 None
    layout object

    Deprecated and ignored; a warning is issued, as in metafor.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    PlotPermutestResult

    A PlotPermutestResult with the fields axes (the axes of the panels drawn) and names ('QM', 'QS' or the
    PlotPermutestResult

    coefficient name of each panel, in the same order).

    Raises:

    Type Description
    InputError

    trim is 0.5 or more; alternative, p2defn or stat is not a valid value; a coefficient name or position in beta or alpha does not exist; no panel is selected.
    Metafor reference

    plot_vif ¶

    plot_vif(
    x: VIFResult,
    breaks: object = 'Scott',
    freq: bool = False,
    col: str | None = None,
    border: str | None = None,
    col_out: str | None = None,
    col_density: str | None = None,
    trim: float = 0.0,
    adjust: float = 1.0,
    lwd: float | Sequence[float] = (2, 0),
    *,
    tail: str = 'upper',
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    layout: object = None,
) -> PlotVifResult

    Plot the simulated (G)VIFs of a vif result obtained with sim=True (plot.vif.rma).

    Mirrors metafor's plot.vif.rma().

    One panel is drawn per (G)VIF in x, titled Coefficient: name (Coefficients: name for a set of coefficients). Each panel is the histogram of the (G)VIFs simulated under independence of the moderators, with the observed (G)VIF as a dashed black vertical line and the bars beyond it filled with col_out. A (G)VIF beyond the right edge of the plot is drawn at the edge, with an arrow pointing to it. The kernel density estimate is omitted by default (its lwd is 0).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    x VIFResult

    The result of vif obtained with sim=True.

    		 required
    breaks object

    The breaks argument of R's hist(): a number of bins, a rule name or a vector of break points. Default: 'Scott'.

    		 'Scott'
    freq bool

    Draw counts instead of densities. This turns off the kernel density estimate. Default: False.

    		 False
    col str | None

    Fill colour of the histogram bars. Default: '#B3B3B3' (light grey).

    		 None
    border str | None

    Border colour of the bars. Default: '#E5E5E5' (lighter grey).

    		 None
    col_out str | None

    Fill colour of the bars beyond the observed (G)VIF. Default: '#FF000080' (semi-transparent red). The observed value itself is always drawn in black.

    		 None
    col_density str | None

    Colour of the kernel density estimate. Default: 'blue'.

    		 None
    trim float

    Fraction (below 0.5) of the largest simulated values dropped from the histogram. Default: 0.

    		 0.0
    adjust float

    Bandwidth adjustment of the kernel density estimate, as the adjust argument of R's density(). Default: 1.

    		 1.0
    lwd float | Sequence[float]

    Line widths of the dashed line at the observed (G)VIF and of the kernel density estimate; a width of 0 leaves the element out. A single number is used for both. Default: (2, 0).

    		 (2, 0)
    tail str

    Tail of the simulated distribution filled beyond the observed (G)VIF, 'upper' or 'lower'. Not in metafor, which always fills the upper tail. Default: 'upper'.

    		 'upper'
    ax Axes | None

    Matplotlib axes to draw into; the panels are laid out inside it. Default: the current axes.

    		 None
    xlim Sequence[float] | None

    Limits of the horizontal axis of every panel. Default: the range of the histogram breaks. The plotted axis extends 4 percent beyond the limits, as in R.

    		 None
    layout object

    Deprecated and ignored; a warning is issued, as in metafor.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    PlotVifResult

    A PlotVifResult with the fields axes (one axes per panel) and names (the coefficient names of the panels).

    Raises:

    Type Description

    x was not obtained with sim=True; trim is 0.5 or more; tail is neither 'lower' nor 'upper'.
